title: Past-only variance-proxy particle allocation under moving bottlenecks: defensive square-root mixing is materially more robust to stale estimates than unhedged Neyman allocation

public_sources.title: Variance estimation in the particle filter
public_sources.used_for: Single-run genealogy-based asymptotic-variance estimation; decomposition into time-step terms v_{p,n}; fixed-budget optimum c_p proportional to sqrt(v_{p,n}); paper reports an outlier-observation example where optimal allocation reduced variance by about a factor of 40. The paper also explicitly notes its non-asymptotic second-moment expression does not apply to non-multinomial resampling.

public_sources.title: Adaptive online variance estimation in particle filters: the ALVar estimator
public_sources.used_for: Genealogy-only online asymptotic-variance monitoring with adaptive lag, average constant-in-time memory/compute for fixed N, and no extra simulation. Published experiments report ALVar about 1.5-2x a standard PF at N=1000 and about 2-2.5x at N=100000, while adapting lag automatically.

public_sources.title: Central limit theorem for the stratified resampling mechanism
public_sources.used_for: Direct CLT evidence for one-step stratified resampling. The paper gives an inductive particle-filter asymptotic-variance formula under a stated conjecture about the corresponding fractional-part convergence at later filtering steps, so it is not treated here as a theorem-level multi-generation single-run variance estimator.

public_sources.title: Adaptive Neyman Allocation
public_sources.used_for: Cross-field precedent that earlier-stage variance observations can guide later-stage Neyman allocations and that the statistical cost of learning an unknown optimal allocation can be analyzed competitively.

public_sources.title: Weighted Average Importance Sampling and Defensive Mixture Distributions
public_sources.used_for: Cross-field precedent for retaining a nominal/base component as insurance against proposal misspecification; used only as analogy for the defensive uniform reserve, not as a proof for particle allocation.

synthetic_drift_model.regime_definition: In regime j in {0,...,4}, generation j uses shock_potential and the other four generations use mild_potential. Regimes cycle 0->1->2->3->4, so the dominant asymptotic variance term moves across generations.
synthetic_drift_model.resampling: Independent stratified uniforms per stratum; no shared-offset systematic variable.

past_only_proxy_and_controller.proxy: At completed run r and generation p, compute H_{p,r}(x)=Q_{p,5}(1)(x) from that synthetic run's known finite-state Feynman-Kac model and use sample CV^2, s^2(H(X_p))/mean(H(X_p))^2, as a one-run plug-in proxy for v_{p,5}=eta_p(H^2)/(eta_p H)^2-1. It is used only after the run completes; no current-run outcome changes the current particle counts.
past_only_proxy_and_controller.proxy_scope: This is an online asymptotic-variance proxy, not a claim that the Lee-Whiteley finite-N genealogy estimator remains exact under stratified resampling.
past_only_proxy_and_controller.estimator_update: Abar_{r+1}=0.4*Abar_r+0.6*proxy_r; schedule for run r+1 is chosen only from Abar_{r+1} after run r has completed.
past_only_proxy_and_controller.defensive_allocation: For beta in [0,1), q_p=(1-beta)/5 + beta*sqrt(Abar_p)/sum_s sqrt(Abar_s), N_p approximately 320*q_p with integer rounding. The validated controller fixes beta=0.5, so every generation retains a 32-particle uniform reserve before the remaining 160 particles are directionally concentrated.
past_only_proxy_and_controller.robustness_bound: Because q_p >= (1-beta)/5 for every p, for any nonnegative true coefficient vector A and any stale/misspecified estimate Abar, sum_p A_p/(320*q_p) <= [1/(1-beta)] * sum_p A_p/64. Thus beta=0.5 gives a crude allocation-mismatch ceiling of 2x the uniform asymptotic variance; beta=0.75 gives 4x. This bound concerns the separable asymptotic objective only, not finite-N stratified PF variance.

exact_stale_schedule_stress.method: Use the exact coefficient vectors above in the separable asymptotic objective sum_p A_p/N_p, but deliberately allocate from another regime's coefficient vector.

beta_0_5.worst_case: true regime 4 with schedule learned from regime 1

unhedged_floor16_KKT.worst_case: true regime 4 with schedule learned from regime 1

exact_stale_schedule_stress.interpretation: More aggressive matched-regime allocation is better when the coefficients are current, but stale estimates can reverse the gain. The defensive uniform reserve makes the mismatch penalty substantially smaller in this drift family.

independent_stream_validation.controller: beta=0.5, EWMA alpha=0.6, total particles=320, independent stratified resampling; each stream cycles through the five regimes three times. Discovery/tuning seeds were disjoint from the validation seeds summarized here.

phase_length_5.scope: Directionally positive but not strong enough here for a conventional 5% two-sided significance claim.

independent_stream_validation.contrast_with_aggressive_unhedged_contro: A separate validation of floor-constrained KKT allocation driven by the same lagged proxy lost about 14.9% versus uniform at phase length 5, was approximately neutral at length 10, and gained about 6.6% at length 20. This is engineering evidence that stale-estimate sensitivity, not the square-root law itself, is the main fast-drift failure mode.

fixed_overhead_latency_rule.derivation: Let asymptotic variance be V=sum_p A_p/N_p, variable compute cost be B=sum_p k_p N_p, and unavoidable per-run overhead be C0=sum_p c0_p. For fixed B, the optimal continuous allocation is N_p = B*sqrt(A_p/k_p)/S where S=sum_s sqrt(A_s k_s), giving V*=S^2/B. To reach a fixed confirmation variance using repeated independent runs, idealized total compute is proportional to V*(C0+B)=S^2*(1+C0/B).
fixed_overhead_latency_rule.diminishing_return: The only overhead penalty after within-run optimal allocation is C0/B. Increasing particle budget cannot improve the asymptotic variable-cost term S^2; it only amortizes fixed overhead.
fixed_overhead_latency_rule.stop_buying_rule: If one is willing to leave at most epsilon fractional overhead relative to variable compute, stop increasing B once C0/B <= epsilon, equivalently B >= C0/epsilon. The maximum remaining latency improvement available from taking B to infinity is C0/(B+C0).
fixed_overhead_latency_rule.fixed_budget_implication: When uniform and adaptive schedules use the same B and same fixed C0, their confirmation-latency ratio is approximately their variance/MSE ratio. Thus the phase-length-20 synthetic result corresponds to about 9.7% lower idealized confirmation time at equal per-run cost; phase-length-50 corresponds to about 11.9%.

negative_scope: The synthetic online proxy uses exact finite-state continuation values H=Q_{p,5}(1); a real agent evaluator generally does not know these and would need an estimated continuation/influence proxy.

Lee-Whiteley's finite-N second-moment estimator is multinomial-resampling specific. The current implementation deliberately keeps stratified resampling for robustness, so the plug-in proxy is not presented as a theorem-level unbiased stratified genealogy estimator.

The 2023 stratified-resampling CLT is direct for the resampling mechanism; its recursive particle-filter variance formula is stated under a conjecture for later steps. This does not close a single-run, multi-generation stratified variance-estimation theorem.

Fast drift can erase or reverse gains if beta is too aggressive. The exact mismatch bound controls only the separable asymptotic allocation model; finite-N interactions and resampling variance can differ.
All numerical gains are for a two-state synthetic Feynman-Kac model. They imply no AGI capability or real-agent benchmark improvement.
Current-run outcome-dependent particle stopping is still outside the predictable-count correctness argument; all schedules here are fixed before the run begins.
frontier: Derive or locate a theorem-clean single-run estimator of generation-wise variance contributions compatible with independent stratified resampling; otherwise separate a multinomial diagnostic pilot from a stratified production estimator and quantify the mismatch.

Replace fixed beta=0.5 by a predictable uncertainty-aware hedge: choose the largest beta whose stale-coefficient uncertainty set keeps a prespecified worst-case inflation bound, then ramp concentration only after stability is certified.
Stress 10-20 generations with moving shocks and genealogy collapse; compare the continuation-value proxy with ALVar-like lagged ancestry statistics and measure detection/adaptation lag.

Extend the fixed-overhead rule to random wall-clock tool costs k_p and parallel descendants; choose N_p proportional to sqrt(A_p/k_p) using past-only cost estimates and evaluate confirmation latency rather than only sample variance.
Map to multi-turn agent trajectories only when base/proposal transition likelihoods, high-fidelity label semantics, and a computable per-generation influence/continuation proxy are explicit.
exact_next_action: Construct a 10-20 generation moving-shock model and implement two past-only diagnostics side by side: (1) the current continuation-value CV^2 proxy and (2) an ALVar-style lagged ancestry dispersion statistic computed from the same stratified particle cloud but treated as heuristic until a stratified theorem is established. Use a predictable uncertainty set over the coefficient vector to choose beta by a worst-case variance-inflation cap, rather than fixing beta=0.5. Evaluate adaptation lag, normalized MSE and fixed-overhead confirmation latency under abrupt, gradual and recurring bottleneck motion. In parallel continue searching for a rigorous stratified single-run variance estimator; do not import multinomial genealogy guarantees unchanged.
